explanation:
In C++, a pure virtual function is a virtual function declared with '= 0' that must be overridden by derived classes. A class containing at least one pure virtual function is considered an abstract class and cannot be instantiated directly. This mechanism enforces interface-like behavior, enabling polymorphism and design of flexible, extensible class hierarchies essential for object-oriented programming.
